Text files, modes and paths

Unit 1 · Week 7 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor, a dedicated disposable practice folder and a text editor. Keep original class data separate.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Text files, modes and paths

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means choose read/write/append deliberately, explain relative paths and preserve one record per line. Use only disposable practice files when demonstrating write mode.

2. Retrieval: keeping values

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and pair explanation

Allow one minute without notes then compare. A list retains values while that program is running; a saved text file can be read in a later run. Traversal visits each item. Ask what information must persist beyond program exit before naming the file format.

3. Three file modes

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked comparison and guided prediction

Read r requires an existing file. Write w creates a missing file or truncates an existing file when opened. Append a creates a missing file or adds at its end. Use an existing practice file containing 2, then ask what w and a would do before executing. with closes the file when its block exits, including after an exception.

4. A path starts from a location

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher demonstration and paired explanation

Explain a relative name is resolved from current working directory, which can differ from script location. Demonstrate the actual school editor setting and locate the practice folder. An absolute path specifies its full location; avoid machine-specific paths in shared examples. Learners point to their folder without editing important files. Missing file in r raises FileNotFoundError.

5. Two records, two lines

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, run, investigate

In the practice folder, w writes 2 followed by newline, then a writes 5 followed by newline. The file contains two records, 2 and 5, not 25. UTF-8 makes text encoding explicit. Predict first, run, inspect with a text editor. Re-running the whole snippet resets the file first because w comes before a; running only append again adds another 5. Emphasise both cases.

6. Reading the records in order

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired coding with role changes

Expected displayed lines 2 and 5, with a third 5 if only append ran again. strip removes surrounding whitespace, including newline, from the string. Driver runs a read; navigator compares actual file contents, then swap and append 0 before reading again. Support: provide with header. Stretch: explain why a file with no final newline can join a later append onto the last record.

7. Which mode preserves earlier records?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question

Correct C:a. w replaces old text and r does not permit writing. Collect simultaneous choices then explain. If several choose w, compare opening w with opening a on two disposable copies. File mode choice matters before any write call.

8. Exit ticket: explain the file contract

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

Expected one non-negative integer per line, consistent UTF-8, newline after each record, a to add and r to read. A relative file path uses working directory. Collect individual explanations; use errors for a short mode/path reminder before validation.
